Caliban has two HTTP surfaces. This page lists every endpoint of both, grouped by what you do with them.

| Surface | Default address | Who calls it | Authentication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway (data plane) | `http://<host>:8080` | Your apps, with OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs or the Caliban SDKs | A workspace API key: `Authorization: Bearer cal_...` |
| Admin API (control plane) | `http://<host>:8081` | The console, the SDK admin clients, scripts | A console session, an access token from your identity provider, or the admin token |

Plain names on this page, API names in code: a workspace is a `tenant`, an assistant is a `node`, a run is one conversation with an assistant, a topic is an `intent`, the data dictionary is the `ontology`, a data connection is a `datasource`, a document library is a `rag` collection. See the [glossary](glossary.md).

Every admin route checks one permission: `401` means you are not signed in, `403` means your roles do not allow it. A successful `DELETE` returns `204` and writes one audit row; a repeat delete is `404`. Errors use one envelope, described in [Errors](errors.md). Response headers of the gateway are in [Response headers](response-headers.md).

The machine-readable contract is `api/openapi.yaml` in the core repository.

## Gateway: send requests

The data plane (port 8080). Apps call it with a workspace API key (`cal_...`).

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI-compatible chat completion (streaming via SSE when stream=true) |
| `POST` | `/v1/messages` | Anthropic Messages API (streaming via SSE when stream=true) |
| `POST` | `/v1/messages/count_tokens` | Approximate input token count for an Anthropic Messages request |
| `GET` | `/v1/models` | Models available to the calling tenant (OpenAI format) |
| `POST` | `/v1/embeddings` | OpenAI-compatible embeddings (open embedding models on-prem, or BYOK providers) |
| `POST` | `/v1/rerank` | Rerank documents against a query (Cohere/Jina-style; e.g. Qwen3-Reranker on vLLM, bge-reranker on TEI) |

### OpenAI-compatible chat completion (streaming via SSE when stream=true)

```http
POST /v1/chat/completions
```

Authenticate with a tenant API key (`cal_…`).

**Nodes.** `model: "node/<name>"` (or `"node/<name>@v<N>"`) runs a published node: the
messages become its input, its output is the assistant message, and a human step is the
assistant message with `finish_reason: "input_required"` (continue with the header
`Caliban-Run-Id` and the answer as the last user message). The body then carries a `caliban`
object (`run_id`, `status`, `node`, `version`, `cost_usd`, `awaiting`). With
`model: "caliban/auto"`, a tenant that maps intents to nodes gets the node when the request
classifies into such an intent (see core/docs/nodes.md).

**Request body:** [ChatCompletionRequest](#chatcompletionrequest)

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Completion, or an SSE stream of `chat.completion.chunk` objects. | [ChatCompletionResponse](#chatcompletionresponse) |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `429` | A rate limit or token budget was exceeded (`[limits]` in the config). `error.type` is `rate_limited`; `error.code` names the limit (`requests_per_minute`, `key_requests_per_minute`, `tokens_per_minute`, `tokens_per_day`, `usd_per_day`). | [Error](#error) |
| `502` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | The PII model's queue is full (`CALIBAN_PII_NER_OVERFLOW=reject`, the default). The request was not sent upstream; retry after `retry-after` seconds. `error.type` is `overloaded`. | [Error](#error) |

### Anthropic Messages API (streaming via SSE when stream=true)

```http
POST /v1/messages
```

Same pipeline as `/v1/chat/completions` (auth, rate limits, PII protect/rehydrate, routing,
cache, fallbacks, metering). Authenticate with `x-api-key: cal_…` (Anthropic SDKs) or a
bearer key. When the routed model's provider is Anthropic the request body is passed
through natively (`cache_control` breakpoints preserved, PII applied to text blocks);
otherwise it is translated to the model's dialect and the response translated back,
including stream events (`message_start`, `content_block_start/delta/stop` with
`text`/`thinking`/`tool_use`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`, `ping`). `thinking` maps to
the Caliban reasoning preference; the optional `caliban` extension is accepted. Errors use
the Anthropic shape (`AnthropicError`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic-version` | header | string | no |  |
| `anthropic-beta` | header | string | no | Forwarded to Anthropic on native passthrough. |

**Request body:** [AnthropicMessagesRequest](#anthropicmessagesrequest)

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | An Anthropic `message`, or an SSE stream of Anthropic events. | [AnthropicMessage](#anthropicmessage) |
| `400` | Error (Anthropic shape) | [AnthropicError](#anthropicerror) |
| `401` | Error (Anthropic shape) | [AnthropicError](#anthropicerror) |
| `403` | Error (Anthropic shape) | [AnthropicError](#anthropicerror) |
| `429` | Rate limit or token budget exceeded (Anthropic shape, `error.type` = `rate_limit_error`). | [AnthropicError](#anthropicerror) |
| `502` | Error (Anthropic shape) | [AnthropicError](#anthropicerror) |
| `503` | The PII model's queue is full (Anthropic shape, `error.type` = `overloaded_error`). Nothing was sent upstream. | [AnthropicError](#anthropicerror) |

### Change a tenant's PII, cache and cache-hit billing settings

```http
PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}
```

Absent fields keep their value; other fields are rejected. Audited as `tenant.update`
(old and new values). Routers apply the change with their next snapshot.
`pii_surrogate_scope: session` opts the tenant out of per-tenant surrogates: every request
gets fresh surrogates (unlinkable), and requests carrying PII bypass the exact and semantic
caches. `semantic_cache: on` lets the tenant's eligible requests use the semantic cache
(also needs `[cache.semantic] enabled`). `auto_cache_hit_fraction` sets the share of the
flat `caliban/auto` price billed for this tenant's cache hits (0 to 1); `null` clears it, so
the deployment's `[routing] auto_cache_hit_fraction` (default 0.2) applies. Out of range
is a 422. `node_caps` bounds the budgets of every node version the tenant publishes (and
promotes); `null` restores the defaults. Lowering the caps does not touch versions already
published, but promoting one that no longer fits is refused.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** [TenantUpdate](#tenantupdate)

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [Tenant](#tenant) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Delete a tenant (tombstone)

```http
DELETE /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}
```

In one audited transaction (`tenant.delete`): the tenant becomes a tombstone
(`status: deleted`, `deleted_at` set), all its API keys are revoked, its BYOK provider
credentials and its data key (DEK) are destroyed (crypto-shredding), its routes are removed, and its
datasources (connection settings wiped) and nodes are soft-deleted. The tenant leaves the
data-plane snapshot, so routers reject its keys from their next snapshot. Audit rows are
kept. The tenant id cannot be reused (`POST /api/v1/tenants` with the same name is a 409).
Every tenant-scoped endpoint returns 404 for a deleted tenant.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Deleted |  |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### List the tenant's Caliban API keys (metadata only)

```http
GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/api-keys
```

Active keys. Revoked keys (with `revoked_at`) are included only with `include_revoked=true`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `include_revoked` | query | boolean (default `false`) | no |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | array of [ApiKeyInfo](#apikeyinfo) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Change an API key's node allowlist and datasource scopes

```http
PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/api-keys/{keyId}
```

Absent fields are kept; `null` lifts a restriction (every published node; every scope of the
nodes it runs). Changing node access needs `nodes.run` on the tenant (`403` otherwise).
Audited as `api_key.update` with the old and new values; routers apply it with their next
snapshot.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `keyId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The key | [ApiKeyInfo](#apikeyinfo) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Revoke a Caliban API key

```http
DELETE /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/api-keys/{keyId}
```

Soft revoke (`api_key.revoke` audit row): the key keeps its row with `revoked_at` set and
its hash leaves the data-plane snapshot. A standalone deployment rejects the key (401) on
the next request; a split-mode router rejects it after its next snapshot poll
(`CALIBAN_SNAPSHOT_POLL_SECS`, default 10 s). A revoked key's hash can never be reused.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `keyId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Revoked |  |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | The tenant's eval key: managed by the control plane (rotate it with `POST .../eval-key/rotate`) | [Error](#error) |

## Data dictionary

The reviewed business names for your data (`ontology`).

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/datasources/{datasourceId}/introspect` | Introspect and profile a source, then propose ontology elements (all with status=proposed) |

| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/ontology/proposals` | Propose ontology elements made outside Caliban (written as proposed, one version) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/ontology` | Current ontology (Caliban Semantic Model) for a tenant |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ontology/elements/{elementId}/review` | Review one ontology element of the tenant named in the body |

| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/ontology/review` | Review a batch of the tenant's ontology elements as one version (ontology.review) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/ontology/elements/{elementId}/review` | Review one of the tenant's ontology elements (a batch of one) |

### Introspect and profile a source, then propose ontology elements (all with status=proposed)

```http
POST /api/v1/datasources/{datasourceId}/introspect
```

The ontology bootstrap (docs/datasources.md): connects with the datasource's credentials, checks the
principal is read only, samples every collection, and writes proposals in one ontology version.
Proposals for elements a human already reviewed, and unchanged ones, are skipped. MongoDB only.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `datasourceId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | Bootstrap job accepted | object |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### The newest introspection job of the datasource (stored; every control-plane replica answers)

```http
GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasourceId}/introspection
```

A job whose control plane stopped before it ended is shown `failed` once it is older than the job timeout (10 minutes) and a minute.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `datasourceId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [IntrospectionJob](#introspectionjob) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Propose ontology elements made outside Caliban (written as proposed, one version)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/ontology/proposals
```

Elements are written as `proposed` in one version, whatever `status` they carry (it may be
left out). An element whose `spec`, `name` and `description` match the tenant's is skipped,
so posting the same model again makes no version and keeps every review decision. A
changed element goes back to `proposed`; over an approved element that withdraws it, which
is refused (`409`) when published node versions query it, unless `acknowledge_breaking`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Written (unchanged elements skipped) | object |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Current ontology (Caliban Semantic Model) for a tenant


### Review a batch of the tenant's ontology elements as one version (ontology.review)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/ontology/review
```

Every decision applies to the tenant's element of that id. The batch is one new ontology
version (none when it changes nothing). A decision that withdraws an approved element that
a published node version's fixed CQIR query touches is a breaking change: `409` naming the
elements and node versions, unless `acknowledge_breaking: true` (those versions then fail on
that query until a version written on the new ontology is published). Approving new
elements, or changing elements no fixed query touches, is compatible: published versions
keep working on the new version. Audited as `ontology.review`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The new version, the reviewed elements, and the breaking changes acknowledged | object |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |

Assistants are `nodes` in the API.

| `POST` | `/v1/runs/{runId}/cancel` | Cancel a node run |
| `POST` | `/mcp` | The MCP server (Streamable HTTP, stateless) |
| `GET` | `/v1/runs/{runId}` | Get a node run |
| `POST` | `/v1/runs/{runId}/input` | Answer the human step a run waits for |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/runs` | The tenant's node runs (console) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/runs/{runId}` | A node run (console) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/runs/{runId}/input` | Answer a question or approve or deny a tainted write (console) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/runs/{runId}/cancel` | Cancel a run (console) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/runs/{runId}/golden-case` | Turn a finished run into a golden case |

| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions` | List the versions of a node |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions` | Create a draft version |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions/{version}` | Get a version (spec and content hash) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions/{version}/publish` | Publish a draft (and promote it by default) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions/{version}/retire` | Retire a published version |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/promote` | Move the promotion pointer (promote or roll back) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/diff` | Diff two versions |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/nodes` | List nodes (AI sub-apps) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/nodes` | Create a draft node version (same as POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions) |

### Run a published node

```http
POST /v1/nodes/{nodeName}/runs
```

Starts a run of the node's live version (or `version`). The API key must be allowed to run
the node (its node allowlist; no allowlist: every published node of the tenant). The input
is checked against the node's `prompt.input_schema`.

**Sync** (default): waits until the run ends or waits for a human, at most the server's
`CALIBAN_NODE_SYNC_WAIT_SECS` (default 60) or `wait_s`; `200` when the run ended, `202`
with the run so far otherwise. **Async** (`"async": true`): `202` at once; poll
`GET /v1/runs/{id}` (also in `Location`).

`Idempotency-Key` (1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, per tenant, kept with the run):
a repeat returns the run the first request created (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and starts
nothing; the same key with another body is a `422` (`idempotency_key_reused`).

**Stream** (`"stream": true`): `200` with the run's events (`text/event-stream`, see
`GET /v1/runs/{runId}/events`) until it ends or waits for a human.

Instead of `input`, `chat.messages` gives chat messages, mapped to the node's input as the
`node/<name>` chat shortcut does.

**Untrusted caller data** (`untrusted`): `true` marks the whole input, a list of JSON
pointers marks fields (`["/email/body"]`). Marked values that are present (and the fields
the node's input schema declares `x-caliban-untrusted: true`, whoever calls) make the run
input carry the `caller` taint label: a write tool their data reaches needs an
`allow_tainted` entry or a human approval, as with tool outputs. Unmarked input is trusted
(the API key that may run the node is the principal). See core/docs/tools.md.

Every model call the run makes goes through the gateway pipeline as the invoking key (PII,
caches, routing, quotas, metering), with an Idempotency-Key per step. Split-mode routers
forward this request to a worker.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nodeName` | path | string | yes |  |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | string | no |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The run ended (succeeded, failed, budget_exhausted or cancelled), or its event stream | [NodeRun](#noderun) |
| `202` | The run is pending, running, sleeping or waiting for input | [NodeRun](#noderun) |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |

| `status` | query | string | no | Comma-separated run statuses |
| `created_after` | query | string | no |  |
| `created_before` | query | string | no |  |
| `limit` | query | integer (default `50`) | no |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [NodeRunList](#noderunlist) |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Follow a run's events (SSE)

```http
GET /v1/runs/{runId}/events
```

The run's events from the journal, numbered from 1, so a client resumes on any worker or
router with `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=`). Each SSE event has `id`, `event` (the type) and
`data` (a `RunEvent`). The stream ends after `run.finished`, or after `run.input_required`
while the run waits for that answer; that last event carries the run in `run`. Events never
carry step content; `run.input_required` carries the question.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `Last-Event-ID` | header | string | no |  |
| `after` | query | integer | no |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The event stream | string |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Cancel a node run

```http
POST /v1/runs/{runId}/cancel
```

Durable: a run that waits (pending, sleeping, input required) is `cancelled` at once (`200`);
a running run is asked to stop (`202`, `cancel_requested: true`) and stops at its next step
boundary on whichever worker runs it (the model call in flight completes and is recorded; a
failing one is not retried). Cancelling a cancelled run is `200`; a run that ended otherwise
is `409` (`run_already_ended`). Audited as `node.run.cancel`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The run is cancelled | [NodeRun](#noderun) |
| `202` | The running run will stop at its next step | [NodeRun](#noderun) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### The MCP server (Streamable HTTP, stateless)

```http
POST /mcp
```

JSON-RPC over Streamable HTTP. Authenticate with the tenant API key as bearer token (`401`
otherwise). `tools/list`: the published nodes the key may run (input schema: the node's).
`tools/call`: runs the node, waits at most `CALIBAN_NODE_SYNC_WAIT_SECS`. With
`CALIBAN_MCP_TASKS=true`, clients declaring the tasks extension get a task (its id is the run
id) and use `tasks/get`, `tasks/update`, `tasks/cancel`. `params._meta["caliban/untrusted"]`
on `tools/call` (`true`, or JSON pointers into the arguments) marks arguments as untrusted
caller data, like `untrusted` on `POST /v1/nodes/{name}/runs`. See core/docs/nodes.md.

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The JSON-RPC answer | object |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Get a node run

```http
GET /v1/runs/{runId}
```

A run of the key's tenant, of a node the key may run.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [NodeRun](#noderun) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Answer the human step a run waits for

```http
POST /v1/runs/{runId}/input
```

Records the answer (sealed in the journal, with who answered: `api_key:<hash prefix>`) and
resumes the run. `step` defaults to the step the run waits for (`awaiting.step`). `409`
(`run_not_awaiting_input`) when the run is not waiting for input, or not for that step.

A step named `<step>@approve` is the approval of a write whose arguments carry untrusted taint
labels: answer `{"approve": true}` or `{"approve": false}` (a refusal fails the call). The
decision is journaled as an `approval` step (see docs/tools.md). Answers and approval decisions
are audited (`node.run.answer`, `node.write.approve`, `node.write.deny`) in the control
plane's hash-chained log, with who answered.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | Accepted; the run resumes | [NodeRun](#noderun) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Turn a finished run into a golden case

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/runs/{runId}/golden-case
```

Production feedback for the eval loop (research note 04, sections 6 and 7). Builds a case
from the run and appends it to the golden set of the run's version (or of `version`, a
version of the same node): the run's input, its human steps' answers as scripted
`answers`, a `json_schema` check when the version has an output schema; for `good`, an
`llm_judge` check with the run's output as `reference` and a `tool_call` check for each
write tool it called; for `bad`, an `llm_judge` check whose rubric is the `note`. The case
id is the run id. The set gets a new hash like an edit (a compare-and-set on the hash read,
so concurrent edits are not lost). A `mast_label` is stored on the run. Needs `nodes.write`
(what editing a golden set needs); the `case` is returned with `runs.data`. Audited as
`node.golden_set.capture` (ids, verdict, label, counts and hashes; never the note or
content). See docs/evals.md ("Cases from runs").

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `runId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** [GoldenCaseCapture](#goldencasecapture)

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Appended | [CapturedGoldenCase](#capturedgoldencase) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | No such run in this tenant (another tenant's run included), or no such version | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | The run has not finished, it is already in that golden set, or the set kept changing | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | `good` on a run that did not succeed, `bad` without a note, a label on `good`, an unknown label, an injection-suite run, or a case that does not fit the set (problems of kind `golden_set`) | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |


changing a node means creating a new version. Needs `nodes.write`; audited as `node.create`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `nodeName` | path | string | yes |  |

| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Publish a draft (and promote it by default)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions/{version}/publish
```

Validates the draft against the tenant: the static checks again; every `node://name@vN` it
calls is a published version of the same tenant and references form no cycle; every
datasource scope (`<datasource>.<object>:<access>`) names a datasource of the tenant and
`*` or an approved ontology entity bound to it; the budgets fit the tenant's
`node_caps`; `mcp://` tools are pinned (resolving them against an approved tool registry
comes with the MCP client). The spec is then sealed under the tenant's data key (created on
first use; needs `CALIBAN_KEK`, else 400) and ships to routers and workers in the signed
snapshot. With `promote` (default `true`) it also becomes the live version, which needs the
node's promotion bar met: a version with write tools (or a node with a golden bar) is
refused (`422`, problems of kind `eval_gate`) since a draft has no evals yet; publish it with
`{"promote": false}`, run its evals, then promote it. Needs `nodes.publish`; audited as
`node.publish` (with the evals that met the bar, under `evals`). A version that is not a
draft is a 409; a validation failure is a 422 listing every problem.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `nodeName` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | path | integer | yes |  |

**Request body:** object (optional)

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Published | [Node](#node) |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Retire a published version

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions/{version}/retire
```

The version leaves the data-plane snapshot: new runs of it are refused (`404`), and runs
already started finish on the version they started on (each run keeps the specs of the
versions it can reach, sealed in the journal). If it was live, the node has no live version
until another is promoted. A version still called (`node://`) by another published version is a 409.
Retirement is final. Needs `nodes.publish`; audited as `node.retire`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `nodeName` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | path | integer | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Retired | [Node](#node) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Move the promotion pointer (promote or roll back)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/promote
```

Makes a published version the live one (what `POST /v1/nodes/{name}/runs` without a version
runs). Its budgets are checked against the tenant's current `node_caps` (422). The node's
promotion bar must be met by the version's latest finished evals (422, problems of kind
`eval_gate`): the golden bar when the node sets one, and for a version with write tools
always an injection eval (default bar: every attack blocked). Every `node://` subnode version
it pins (down the tree) must pass its own gate too (problem `path`: `node://<child>@v<N>`;
evidence under `subnodes`). A draft or a retired version is a 409. Needs `nodes.publish`; audited as `node.promote` with the previous live version
and the evals that met the bar (`evals`).

| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `nodeName` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Promoted | [Node](#node) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Start an eval of a published version

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/nodes/{nodeName}/versions/{version}/evals
```

`golden`: every case of the version's golden set (or `cases`) runs `k` times (default 3) as
ordinary node runs on workers, through the request pipeline, as the tenant's eval key (created
and managed by the control plane, see `GET .../eval-key`), or as the API key `api_key_id`
when one is named (it must be active and allowed to run the node). The key's quotas apply and
its usage is metered. Trial runs (origin `eval:<eval>:<case>`) never reach a real write
tool: every call to a tool with effect `write` goes to the eval sandbox, which answers the
case's `tool_results` or a synthetic result marked `"sandbox": true`; reads call the real
tools unless scripted.
`injection`: the built-in injection suite against sandboxed tools (`k` default 1); the run
input is `input`, else the input of `input_case` (or the golden set's first case), whose
checks then measure utility under attack. Needs `nodes.run`; audited as `node.eval.start`.
A version that is not published is a 409.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `nodeName` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | path | integer | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | Started | [Eval](#eval) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Register an MCP tool server (tools.write)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/tool-servers
```

Registering a server is what allows node tools to reach it (the egress allowlist). The URL must be
Streamable HTTP (`http` or `https`; stdio servers are not supported) and pass the egress rules (no
link-local or metadata addresses; loopback only with `CALIBAN_MCP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`). `credential` is
sealed under the tenant's data key at once and never returned. Audited (`tool_server.create`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** [ToolServerCreate](#toolservercreate)

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Created | [ToolServer](#toolserver) |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Change a tool server (tools.write)

```http
PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/tool-servers/{server}
```

Absent fields are kept. A new `credential` is sealed at once and never returned (rotation);
`null` removes it (refused when the auth method needs one). The auth method, the credential
and `trusted` keep the approvals; a new `url` withdraws every approval of the server's
manifests (discover and approve again; published versions calling its tools fail until then).
The URL (and an OAuth token URL) must pass the egress rules (`422`). Audited as
`tool_server.update`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `server` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The server | object |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Delete a tool server (tools.write)


Soft delete; its credential is wiped and its tools leave the data plane. `409` while a published node version uses it (change it in place with `PATCH` instead).

### Approve a manifest by pin (tools.approve)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/tool-servers/{server}/tools/{tool}/approve
```

Only approved manifests reach the data plane and can be pinned by a published node version. A manifest
with scan findings needs `acknowledge_findings: true` (`422` otherwise). Audited (`tool.approve`, with the
findings, the acknowledgement and the network decision). `network` records whether the tool reaches the
network through its arguments (a URL, a host): a read through such a tool is gated like a write (tainted
arguments need an `allow_tainted` entry or a human approval). Absent: the input schema's hints decide
(`network_hint` on the manifest). To change it, revoke and approve again.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `server` | path | string | yes |  |
| `tool` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Approved; `ref` is what node specs pin | object |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |


|---|---|---|---|---|

| Status | Meaning | Body |

### The public keys tool servers verify minted tool tokens with

```http
GET /.well-known/caliban-tool-jwks.json
```

The current and previous `CALIBAN_TOOL_TOKEN_*` public keys (RFC 8037 OKP, Ed25519, `alg: EdDSA`). Tokens are
minted per call, audience-bound (the server's audience), scoped to one tool (`scope: tool:<name>`) and live
60 seconds. Empty without a key.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | JWKS | object |

A collection is what nodes search with `builtin://rag_search`, named in their scopes as

provider or a shared one); it is fixed for the collection's life. `rerank_model` (a catalogue rerank

### Ingest a document (rag.write)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/rag/collections/{collection}/documents
```

Adds a version of `doc_id` (`version` = the previous one + 1). The content (with its title) is sealed under
the tenant's data key at once and never returned. The version is `pending` and **invisible** until a
worker has indexed it and its checks passed: chunking with heading paths, the injection scan, a
near-duplicate check for untrusted sources, personal data pseudonymised before embedding. Then it is
`ready` (and replaces the previous version in one step), or `quarantined` (invisible until released), or
`failed`. Markdown, HTML and plain text; PDF is refused (`422`): convert it first. At most 5 MB of text.
Ingesting the same content and settings as the newest version again changes nothing (`200`,
`unchanged: true`). Audited (`rag.document.ingest`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `collection` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** [RagDocumentIngest](#ragdocumentingest)

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The same content was already there | object |
| `202` | A new pending version | object |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Every version of a document, newest first (rag.read)

```http
GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/rag/collections/{collection}/documents/{docId}
```

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `collection` | path | string | yes |  |
| `docId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | object |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Delete every version of a document (rag.write)

```http
DELETE /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/rag/collections/{collection}/documents/{docId}
```

It stops being served at once and its sealed content is wiped; workers then delete its vectors. Audited (`rag.document.delete`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `collection` | path | string | yes |  |
| `docId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Deleted |  |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Release a quarantined version (rag.approve)

```http
POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/rag/collections/{collection}/documents/{docId}/release
```

A decision about the findings it was quarantined for: `acknowledge_findings` must be `true` (`422`
otherwise). The version goes back to `pending`, is indexed again with its findings acknowledged and served
once ready. `409` when the version is not quarantined. Audited (`rag.document.release`, with the findings).
Released text is still labelled `retrieved` in node runs: a tainted write it inspires needs an allowlist
entry or a human approval.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |
| `collection` | path | string | yes |  |
| `docId` | path | string | yes |  |

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The version, pending again | [RagDocument](#ragdocument) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `409` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `422` | Error | [Error](#error) |

## Usage and audit

Usage events, totals and the audit log.

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/node-spend` | The tenant's node spend today and this month, against its caps |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/usage` | Recent usage events and aggregate savings |

### The tenant's node spend today and this month, against its caps

```http
GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/node-spend
```

What the tenant's node runs spent on model calls (USD, priced like the metering) today and
this month (UTC), across every worker, from the node journal (`503` without one), next to
its `node_spend_caps`. Permission `usage.read`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenantId` | path | string | yes |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | object |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Recent usage events and aggregate savings

```http
GET /api/v1/usage
```

With the Postgres store, from `usage_event`: every data plane's events (split-mode routers ship theirs
through `POST /api/v1/usage/ingest`), totals over all of them, including the days rolled up into
`usage_daily` once raw events pass `CALIBAN_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` (the totals do not change). With the
in-memory store, the last 10,000 events of the process. `node` and `run_id` filter node calls; `by_node`
totals each node version (cost per node); a `run_id` covers raw events only. `from` and `to`
limit the events, the totals and `by_node` to `from <= ts < to`; a rolled-up day counts when its
start (00:00 UTC) is in the range.

**Routing decisions are content-class** (which intent requests go to reveals topics, arXiv
2610.09981): events come without `intent`, `intent_confidence`, `route_stage`, `route` and
`route_fallback` (empty or absent), and `by_route` counts requests per tenant, UTC day, intent,
deciding stage and fallback reason instead (not with `node` or `run_id`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant_id` | query | string | no |  |
| `node` | query | string | no |  |
| `run_id` | query | string | no |  |
| `from` | query | string | no | Events at or after this time (RFC 3339) |
| `to` | query | string | no | Events before this time; `400` unless after `from` |
| `limit` | query | integer (default `100`) | no |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [UsageReport](#usagereport) |

Health, keys, users, roles and the split-mode endpoints.

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/health` | Liveness and build info |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/audit` | Tamper-evident audit log (newest first) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/keys/status` | KEK rotation status (the same report as `caliban keys status`) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/usage/ingest` | Usage events from a split-mode router |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/audit/ingest` | Run decisions from the data plane |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/snapshot` | Signed data-plane config snapshot (split mode; for routers) |

### Liveness and build info

```http
GET /api/v1/health
```

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [Health](#health) |

### Tamper-evident audit log (newest first)

```http
GET /api/v1/audit
```

One row per control-plane mutation. `hash = sha256(prev_hash ‖ canonical_json({seq, ts, tenant_id, actor,
action, target, detail}))` with sorted keys, no whitespace, `ts` in RFC 3339 UTC with microseconds, and 32 zero
bytes as `prev_hash` for the first row. `chain_verified` re-checks the returned window. Never contains secrets.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | integer (default `100`) | no |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [AuditLog](#auditlog) |

### KEK rotation status (the same report as `caliban keys status`)

```http
GET /api/v1/keys/status
```

Which KEK wraps each tenant data key and seals each shared provider key, what still waits for migration,
whether the retired keys in `CALIBAN_KEK_PREVIOUS` are still needed by stored data
(`previous_keks_still_needed`), and what each split-mode router reported on its last snapshot poll
(`routers`: `active` when seen within 10 minutes, `snapshot_version`, `snapshot_kek_ids`, `keyring`,
`needs_previous_kek`, `has_current_kek`). `routers_on_previous_keks` lists the active routers whose snapshot
still needs a retired KEK; `rotation_complete` is true when neither stored data nor an active router does,
which is when `CALIBAN_KEK_PREVIOUS` can be removed. Needs `audit.read`.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | object |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Usage events from a split-mode router

```http
POST /api/v1/usage/ingest
```

Authenticated with the router token (`CALIBAN_ROUTER_TOKEN`), not the admin token. Each `request_id` is
stored once: a batch sent again (lost acknowledgement, router restart) is answered with `duplicates` and
not counted again. Invalid events (empty or oversized ids) are counted as `rejected` and dropped. Billing
fields are stored as the router computed them.

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Stored | object |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `413` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Run decisions from the data plane

```http
POST /api/v1/audit/ingest
```

Authenticated with the router token. Workers deliver the decisions made on the data plane
(`node.run.answer`, `node.write.approve`, `node.write.deny`, `node.run.cancel`,
`node.eval.finish`) at least once; each event id is recorded once in the hash-chained audit
log, so a retry appends nothing. Every other action, including the control plane's own
(`rag.*`, `node.golden_set.*`, `node.eval_policy.update`, `node.eval.start`,
`node.eval.cancel`), is counted as `rejected` and not recorded.

**Request body:** object

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Recorded | object |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Signed data-plane config snapshot (split mode; for routers)

```http
GET /api/v1/snapshot
```

Authenticated with the router token (`CALIBAN_ROUTER_TOKEN`), not the admin token. Enabled only when the
control plane has `CALIBAN_SNAPSHOT_SIGNING_KEY` and `CALIBAN_ROUTER_TOKEN`. The ETag is a digest of the
config; send it back in `If-None-Match` to get 304 while nothing changed. Verify `signature` (Ed25519 over
`"caliban-snapshot-v1\0" ‖ base64-decoded payload`) before parsing `payload`. Sealed BYOK keys stay sealed.

Routers check in with every poll through the `x-caliban-router-*` headers (what they serve); the control
plane records them for `GET /api/v1/keys/status`. Polls without `x-caliban-router-id` are not recorded.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `If-None-Match` | header | string | no |  |
| `x-caliban-router-id` | header | string | no | The router's id (`CALIBAN_ROUTER_ID`, else its host name); 1 to 128 of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`. |
| `x-caliban-router-snapshot` | header | string | no | Version label of the snapshot the router serves. |
| `x-caliban-router-snapshot-kek-ids` | header | string | no | Comma-separated `kek_ids` of the snapshot the router serves. |
| `x-caliban-router-keyring` | header | string | no | Comma-separated ids of the router's own keyring, current KEK first. |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [SignedSnapshot](#signedsnapshot) |
| `304` | Unchanged since the given ETag |  |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `503` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Start single sign-on (browser navigation)

```http
GET /auth/login
```

Redirects (303) to the identity provider (authorization code flow with PKCE) and sets a short-lived
login cookie. On failure to reach the provider, redirects to `/#/login?error=idp_unavailable`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `return_to` | query | string | no | Path on the console to come back to (same origin only), e.g. `/#/tenants`. |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `303` | To the identity provider |  |
| `404` | Error | [Error](#error) |

### Identity provider redirect target (browser navigation)

```http
GET /auth/callback
```

Validates the state, the login cookie and the ID token, creates the session cookie (HttpOnly,
SameSite=Strict) and redirects (303) to `return_to`. Failures redirect to
`/#/login?error=login_failed` (audited as `auth.login_failed`) or `/#/login?error=login_expired`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | query | string | no |  |
| `state` | query | string | no |  |
| `error` | query | string | no |  |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `303` | To the console |  |

### End the console session

```http
POST /auth/logout
```

Needs `X-CSRF-Token`. Clears the cookie; audited as `auth.logout`.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Logged out | object |
| `400` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |
| `403` | Error | [Error](#error) |


| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | OK | [Me](#me) |
| `401` | Error | [Error](#error) |

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |  |

| `semantic_cache` | `off`, `on` | no | T2 semantic cache for this tenant. `on`: eligible requests may be answered with the response to an earlier, semantically similar request of the same tenant (per-entry learned thresholds, deployment error budget). Entries never cross tenants. Also needs `[cache.semantic] enabled`. |
| `pii_patterns` | array of [PiiPattern](#piipattern) | no | Only for callers with `tenant.write` on the tenant (the dictionary may hold staff or customer names); others get `pii_patterns_count`. |
| `pii_dictionary` | array of [PiiTerm](#piiterm) | no | Only for callers with `tenant.write` on the tenant; others get `pii_dictionary_count`. |
| `pii_patterns_count` | integer | no | How many patterns the tenant has (every caller) |
| `pii_dictionary_count` | integer | no | How many dictionary terms the tenant has (every caller) |
| `pii_on_sovereign` | boolean | no | The tenant's PII mode also applies to models inside the trust boundary (`t0_sovereign`, `t1_attested`). Off by default: those models receive the text as is. External models always get the mode; a request's `caliban.pii_floor` (a node's `guardrails.pii`) applies to every model class. |
| `pii_surrogate_scope` | `tenant`, `session` | no | Surrogate consistency for reversible PII. `tenant`: the same value always gets the same surrogate in this tenant (keyed HMAC per tenant, derived from CALIBAN_KEK), so pseudonymised requests can hit the exact cache; sessions of the tenant become linkable through their surrogates. `session`: fresh surrogates per request. Surrogates never cross tenants. |
| `auto_cache_hit_fraction` | number or null | no | Share of the flat `caliban/auto` price billed when a cache tier (exact or semantic) answers this tenant's request: no model is called. `null`: the deployment's `[routing] auto_cache_hit_fraction` (default 0.2) applies. |
| `node_caps` | [NodeCaps](#nodecaps) or null | no | `null`: the defaults (steps 200, tokens 2000000, wall_clock_s 3600, depth 5, fanout 32). |
| `node_spend_caps` | [NodeSpendCaps](#nodespendcaps) or null | no | Caps on what the tenant's node runs spend on model calls; `null`: none. |
| `node_routes` | [NodeRoutes](#noderoutes) | no |  |
| `created_at` | string | yes |  |
| `status` | `active`, `deleted` | no | `deleted` only appears with `include_deleted=true`. |
| `deleted_at` | string or null | no |  |

### PiiPattern

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | yes | Case-insensitive (stored as sent, used upper-cased: `phone` is `PHONE`). NATIONAL_ID, PHONE, EMAIL, PERSON, ORG, LOCATION, IBAN or CARD (and the aliases ID, NATIONALID, NAME, ORGANIZATION, ADDRESS) use the built-in surrogates; other labels are custom (shape-preserving surrogates; masked as `[LABEL]` upper-cased). |
| `pattern` | string | yes | A regex in the Rust regex crate's syntax (linear time: no backreferences or lookaround); must not match the empty string. |

### NodeRoutes

Intents `caliban/auto` hands to the tenant's nodes: intent id to `node/<name>` (the live
version), `node/<name>@published` (the same) or `node/<name>@v<N>`. Overrides
`[routing.tenants.<id>.routes]` of the config file, intent by intent. On update: `null`
clears it, absent keeps it.

### NodeSpendCaps

Caps on what the tenant's node runs spend on model calls (USD, priced like the metering), per
UTC day and month, across all workers: checked before every model call against the journal's
per-day totals. A cap reached ends runs gracefully (`budget_exhausted`).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `daily_usd` | number | no |  |
| `monthly_usd` | number | no |  |

### MastLabel

A MAST failure mode (arXiv 2503.13657): FM-1.1 to FM-1.5 (specification), FM-2.1 to FM-2.6 (inter-agent misalignment), FM-3.1 to FM-3.3 (task verification)

One of `disobey_task_specification`, `disobey_role_specification`, `step_repetition`, `loss_of_conversation_history`, `unaware_of_termination_conditions`, `conversation_reset`, `fail_to_ask_for_clarification`, `task_derailment`, `information_withholding`, `ignored_other_agent_input`, `reasoning_action_mismatch`, `premature_termination`, `no_or_incomplete_verification`, `incorrect_verification`.

### UsageEvent

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | string | yes |  |
| `tenant_id` | string | yes |  |
| `model` | string | yes |  |
| `prompt_tokens` | integer | yes |  |
| `completion_tokens` | integer | yes |  |
| `cached_prompt_tokens` | integer | no | Part of prompt_tokens read from the provider prompt cache. |
| `cache_write_tokens` | integer | no | Part of prompt_tokens written to the provider prompt cache (Anthropic `cache_creation_input_tokens`). Omitted when 0. |
| `cache_write_1h_tokens` | integer | no | Part of cache_write_tokens written with the Anthropic 1-hour TTL. Omitted when 0. |
| `usage_source` | `provider`, `estimated` | no | `provider`: the token counts are the provider's usage report. `estimated`: no complete report arrived (the client disconnected mid-stream, the upstream stream failed or ended without usage, or the model has `rejects_stream_options`), so the gateway estimated them: prompt tokens from the provider's partial report when one arrived (Anthropic `message_start`), else from the request; completion tokens from the output streamed so far, about 4 bytes per token. After a disconnect the provider may bill more than the estimate. Absent on cache hits (nothing consumed) and on events written before this field existed. |
| `tokens_saved` | integer | no | Tokens not sent upstream thanks to Caliban: on a cache hit of either tier, the cached answer's prompt plus completion tokens |
| `intent` | string | no | Always empty in reports (routing decisions are content-class; see `by_route`). Set only in transit, from a data plane. |
| `cache` | `hit`, `miss`, `bypass` | yes |  |
| `cache_tier` | `exact`, `semantic` | no | Only on hits: which cache tier answered. |
| `pii_entities` | integer | no |  |
| `cost_usd` | number or null | no | Uncached prompt tokens at price_in_per_mtok, cache reads at price_cache_read_per_mtok, cache writes at price_cache_write_per_mtok (1-hour writes at price_cache_write_1h_per_mtok), completion at price_out_per_mtok. Unset cache prices fall back to the input price. Null when the model has no input or output price. |
| `latency_ms` | integer | yes |  |
| `ts` | string | yes |  |
| `requested_model` | string | no | Model the client asked for (`caliban/auto` or a pinned id). Chat requests only; absent otherwise. |
| `intent_confidence` | number | no | In transit only (never in reports): confidence of the intent decision, 0..1. |
| `route_stage` | `rules`, `knn`, `keyword` | no | In transit only (never in reports): the stage that decided the intent; counted in `by_route`. |
| `routed_model_cost_usd` | number | no | `caliban/auto` only: real cost of the routed model for this request (the same number and cost function as `cost_usd`, prompt-cache prices included). Absent when the model has no price. |
| `flat_price_usd` | number | no | `caliban/auto` only: flat auto price for the same tokens (`[routing] auto_price_*`), through the same cost function as `cost_usd`; the flat price has no cache prices, so cache reads and writes count at its input price. On a cache hit of either tier: the full flat price of the cached answer's tokens (what a miss would have billed), recorded next to `billed_usd`. Events written before cache-hit billing record 0 on hits. |
| `billed_usd` | number | no | `caliban/auto` only: what the customer is billed. `flat_price_usd` on a miss; on a cache hit of either tier, `flat_price_usd` x the tenant's cache-hit fraction (`auto_cache_hit_fraction`, default 0.2). Margin = billed_usd - routed_model_cost_usd. Absent on events written before cache-hit billing (they billed `flat_price_usd`). |
| `saved_usd` | number | no | Cache hits only: what the hit saved the customer. `caliban/auto`: `flat_price_usd - billed_usd`. Other models: the model cost the hit avoided (the cached answer's tokens at the input and output price; nothing reached the provider). Absent on misses and for unpriced models. |
| `node` | string | no | Node model calls only: the node of the run (its root node: a subnode's calls are the run's). |
| `node_version` | integer | no |  |
| `run_id` | string | no |  |
| `route` | string | no | In transit only (never in reports): the path a caliban/auto request took |
| `route_fallback` | string | no | In transit only (never in reports): why a model answered rather than a node; counted in `by_route` |
| `purpose` | `rag.ingest`, `rag.search` | no | Work Caliban did on the tenant's behalf: `rag.ingest` (embedding a collection's documents), `rag.search` (a node's retrieval query, its embedding and reranking). Absent for client calls and node model calls. Kept in reports (billing-class, not content-class). |
| `timings` | [UsageTimings](#usagetimings) | no |  |

### UsageTimings

Per-stage durations of the request in milliseconds (the `Server-Timing` header's numbers; for streams `upstream_total_ms` and `total_ms` run to the end of the stream). A stage that did not run is absent. Durations only: the deciding routing stage is content-class and not kept. Absent on events written before this field existed (migration 0036).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth_ms` | number | no | Authentication and the rate-limit check. |
| `route_ms` | number | no | Classification and model choice, `embed_ms` included. |
| `embed_ms` | number | no | The routing embedder call (Stage-1 kNN). |
| `pii_ms` | number | no | PII screening. |
| `cache_ms` | number | no | Cache lookups (exact, then semantic). |
| `upstream_ms` | number | no | Upstream model: time to its response headers (first byte). |
| `upstream_total_ms` | number | no | Upstream model: the whole call, to the end of the body or stream. |
| `total_ms` | number | no | Request start to the usage event. |

### Permission

One of `tenants.create`, `catalog.read`, `catalog.write`, `providers.probe`, `audit.read`, `rbac.read`, `rbac.write`, `tenant.read`, `tenant.write`, `tenant.delete`, `api_keys.read`, `api_keys.write`, `provider_keys.read`, `provider_keys.write`, `routes.read`, `routes.write`, `datasources.read`, `datasources.write`, `ontology.read`, `ontology.review`, `nodes.read`, `nodes.write`, `nodes.publish`, `nodes.run`, `tools.read`, `tools.write`, `tools.approve`, `rag.read`, `rag.write`, `rag.approve`, `runs.read`, `runs.data`, `runs.answer`, `usage.read`.

### SignedSnapshot

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key_id` | string | yes | First 16 hex chars of sha256(public key) |
| `payload` | string | yes | base64 of JSON {version, issued_at_ms, config, kek_ids}; config has the caliban.toml structure. kek_ids (omitted when empty) lists the KEKs (`kek_` fingerprints) that sealed the secrets in config: what a router needs in its keyring to open them. |
| `signature` | string | yes | base64 Ed25519 signature |
